title: Havens of the Final Nights
summary: A survey of unusual places where Kindred make their lairs.

claims.text: Not every sire supplies a childe with wealth or a home; childer left on their own must find a haven themselves, and many come out stronger for it.
A haven gives safety and stability, but some Kindred cannot stay shut away and look for security while travelling.

title: Eric Parker
summary: A young Setite who built a haven without help from a sire.

claims.text: Eric Parker was a casino dealer in life, gifted at keeping losing gamblers at the tables.
Eric Parker is offered as an example of a childe who made a way without a wealthy sire.

title: The Glass House
summary: The haven of a former stage illusionist.

claims.text: Jesse Van Reginald, who lives there, came of age around the middle of the 20th century admiring stage magicians such as Blackstone, Dunninger and Houdini, and learned the craft alone.
The haven borrows from stage illusion, using hidden hinged mirrors of the kind once used to make a caged elephant seem to vanish.

title: The House of Storms
summary: A haven whose owner is drawn to the young.

claims.text: Its resident, Kathryn Green, made a fortune in the 1987 stock market crash by buying while others sold.
The haven is built around the pull that youth exerts on the old and worn out.

title: Conrad Constantinos
summary: A wandering Ravnos with a haven on the move.

claims.text: Conrad Constantinos is a Ravnos loner and nomad, moving from city to city out of wanderlust and hunger.
Nearly a century of unlife has made Conrad Constantinos well able to fight.

title: Miss Tara Sunshine
summary: A Brujah with a haven devoted to watching desire.

claims.text: The Brujah known as Miss Tara Sunshine was once Tabitha Somerset, raised on a father's estate in Victorian New England.
The haven plays on the modern taste for watching rather than taking part, which mirrors how Kindred must hold back among mortals.

title: USS Carl Vinson
summary: An aircraft carrier that hides an Assamite.

claims.text: A carrier holds a crew of over 6,000 and works like a small town at sea.
A vampire can survive aboard only through excellent concealment, since odd behaviour among officers would quickly be noticed.
Burak, a 900-year-old Ottoman Turk, former Sufi and Assamite ascetic of strong will, makes a lair in the ship's depths.
